First, we fill the table. Given a value of $x,$ we can find the corresponding $y$ by substituting $x$ into the formula $y=3x-2.$
Therefore,

- if $x=0$ then $y=3(0)-2=-2,$

- if $x=1$ then $y=3(1)-2=1,$

- if $x=2$ then $y=3(2)-2=4,$ and

- if $x=3$ then $y=3(3)-2=7.$

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-2$ | $1$ | $4$ | $7$ |

We plot these $(x,y)$ pairs on the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14165840/assets/09e670353b2114b229769e2bd6b3eb4a9895389b818fc3f4ace6997a3e7efa3f.png)

Finally, connecting the points gives us a straight line. This is the graph of $y=3x-2.$
